messages:
alyssa: Heads up — SCIM onboarding failing for tenant acme-prod. Started right after yesterday's RBAC role-id rename. Provisioner shows 422 and a KMS unwrap error. Anyone seen this pattern?
security-bot: alert: scim.provision.failures spike (tenant=acme-prod) :warning: rate=18/m since 12:03 UTC
sam: Can you paste the raw error lines from the provisioner logs?
alyssa: ```json
2026-03-23T12:04:12Z ERROR provisioner request_id=abcd1234 tenant=acme-prod action=CreateUser error="jwe: unwrap failed: kms:invalid-keyid (kid=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/scim-wrap-v2)"
2026-03-23T12:04:13Z WARN provisioner role_attach user=alice@acme.com role_id=role_0x7f created_orphan=true
```
sam: That kid looks like it points to the new key alias. We rotated keys yesterday during the RBAC rename rollout, right?
mike: Confirming — we rotated the scim-wrap key alias at 2026-03-22T22:40 UTC as part of the role-id rename change. Private customers (Redwood Private) have a local KMS cache in the provisioner service that wasn't invalidated. If the provisioner still had the old wrapping key cached, JWE unwraps will fail when clients use the new kid.
alyssa: But why are we seeing orphaned roles? The role_attach shows created_orphan=true — looks like user creation partially succeeded but role lookup failed.
mike: Likely flow: SCIM create succeeds (user record), then role assignment does a lookup by role_id/name mapping which changed as part of RBAC rename. Provisioner attempted to encrypt role entitlement payload with new kid but couldn't unwrap, so the assignment step failed, leaving the user created without the expected role.
sam: Repro steps we should run: 1) try creating a test user against staging tenant with the new key alias; 2) tail provisioner logs with --include-kms-debug; 3) check provisioner key cache TTL and alias mapping.
ops-bot: deploybot: rollout scim-provisioner v3.2.1 completed to canary at 2026-03-23T11:50 UTC (no errors).
mike: Quick mitigation: revert the RBAC role-id rename mapping in the config-store (hotfix) to restore the previous role_id -> alias mapping, and flush the provisioner KMS cache. Command we used: `ssh jump@prod-provisioner 'sudo systemctl restart provisioner && curl -XPOST localhost:9000/cache/keys/flush'`
alyssa: Performed the rollback for acme-prod mapping at 12:18 UTC and restarted provisioner.
sam: After restart, can you run a dry-run create? `./scripts/scim/provision.sh --tenant acme-prod --dry-run --email test+scim@acme.com`
alyssa: Ran dry-run at 12:22 — success. Then attempted full create and assignment; result: user created and role attached.
security-bot: info: post-mitigation failure rate returned to baseline (2/m) for tenant=acme-prod
mike: Root cause summary for the ticket: concurrent RBAC role-id rename + KMS alias rotation without cache invalidation in private provisioner caused JWE unwrap errors during role assignment, leaving orphaned entitlements. Short-term fix: rollback mapping + restart provisioner. Medium-term: add alias-change watch and key-cache TTLs + an automated backfill that re-applies missing role attachments. Long-term: make SCIM role attachment idempotent and tolerate transient KMS unwrap errors (retry + dead-letter queue).
alyssa: Filed SEC-9876 with steps, logs, and remediation runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-9876
sam: Also add an alert refinement: trigger on 'jwe: unwrap failed' with spikes >5/m for any single tenant — paging to eng-oncall.
mike: I pushed a small patch to the provisioner (PR #4567) to surface KMS kid mismatch in metrics and expose a `/cache/keys/flush` endpoint, plus reduce default key cache TTL from 10m to 30s for canary deployments.
alyssa: Verified production for acme-prod: 10 successful provisioning flows in a row at 12:40 UTC. No new orphaned roles found. :tada:
ops-bot: note: scheduled backfill job scim-reapply-roles for acme-prod in 1h (dry-run available).
alyssa: Thanks all — adding follow-up tasks to SEC-9876: backfill, metrics alert, config rollback playbook, and longer-term idempotency plan.
